title: fix(i18n): the build-history row states its item count in each pack's grammar (objectui#9266)
body:
Fixes #9266

## The defect, measured rather than derived

The commit-history row composed its count by concatenation: `CommitTimeline`
rendered `c.itemCount` itself and then asked `preview.history.items` for a bare
unit word to sit beside it. A pack that never sees the number cannot agree with
it — the agreement lives in a seam no translator owns.

The card derived the breakage from the call site and the pack values and said so
explicitly; nobody had run it. That is the first deliverable here. Rendered
through a real `I18nProvider`, all ten packs, at `itemCount === 1`:

| pack | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| en | `1 item(s)` | `1 item(s)` |
| zh | `1 项` | `1 项` |
| ja | `1 件` | `1 件` |
| ko | `1 항목` | `1 항목` |
| de | `1 Elemente` | `Elemente: 1` |
| fr | `1 éléments` | `Éléments : 1` |
| es | `1 elementos` | `Elementos: 1` |
| pt | `1 itens` | `Itens: 1` |
| ru | `1 элементов` | `Элементов: 1` |
| ar | `1 عناصر` | `العناصر: 1` |

The card's six/four split **holds**: `de` `es` `fr` `pt` `ru` `ar` were
ungrammatical at one item, `en` `ja` `ko` `zh` were not. Nothing in premise 1
had to be corrected.

The same render also found one thing the card did not claim: **`ru` is wrong at
3 as well** (`3 элементов`, where Russian's `few` needs `элемента`). That
reading is what decides the route below, so it is stated here rather than left
in a log.

## The route taken, and why — route 3

`preview.history.items` now carries the count itself, one interpolated value per
pack, and the call site passes `count` instead of printing the digit beside the
translation. Each pack states the quantity in an idiom whose grammar does not
bend on the number. This is the repair `fields.textarea.charactersRemaining`
already carries, with its reasoning written into the `en` pack beside it.

**Why not route 1 (a real plural family).** Measured against a live i18next
instance rather than argued. `all-locales-key-parity` requires identical key
sets across the ten packs, so a family here can only ever be base + `_one` +
`_other`: `ru` may have no `_few`, `ar` no `_two` / `_many`, and every category a
pack does not spell out falls through to the base key. What that renders:

```
ru n= 1 cat=one   -> "1 элемент"     ✅ correct
ru n= 2 cat=few   -> "2 элементов"    ❌ still wrong
ru n= 3 cat=few   -> "3 элементов"    ❌ still wrong
ru n= 5 cat=many  -> "5 элементов"    ✅
ar n= 1 cat=one   -> "1 عنصر"         ✅ correct
ar n= 2 cat=two   -> "2 عناصر"        ❌ dual
ar n=11 cat=many  -> "11 عناصر"       ❌
en/de/es/fr/pt/zh/ja/ko                ✅ fully correct
```

Route 1 repairs eight packs completely and leaves the two packs that motivated
objectui#3863 wrong at everyday counts — and 2 to 4 items is the modal size of a
build change. The count-invariant phrase is correct at **every** count in every
pack, which is why it wins here.

**Why not route 2 (a per-pack count-agnostic unit word).** There is no such word
in the six broken languages that is not either a parenthesised marker — which
the sibling pin's Unicode marker census forbids outside `en`, on measured
grounds — or an abbreviation.

**The number is kept.** objectui#9170 dropped it for `kanban.columns` because a
board's lanes are visible anyway. In a commit row the count is the only thing
saying how much a build changed, so dropping it would delete information rather
than de-duplicate it. That reasoning is read, not its answer.

## The negative control

`en` `zh` `ja` `ko` render **byte-identically to before, at every count**. The
three CJK packs mark no plural; `en`'s value already carried the count-invariant
`(s)` marker and `en` is exempt from the marker census by that census's own
design. No copy that was already correct has been changed — including `ko`,
whose `common.itemCount` counter 개 could now be adopted (the call-site spacing
that blocked it is gone) and deliberately is not, because `ko` was never broken.

## The two pins on this key, both re-derived

The key was pinned in **two** files, not one. The card named only the first.

- `residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx` asserted `ru`'s bare genitive plural
  `элементов` as correct, and its comment offered this key as evidence that the
  bare-unit-word shape "still exists elsewhere". ⚠️ That comment is part of how
  the shape propagated — it vouches for the structure the next author copies —
  so it is rewritten to state what the kanban ruling was actually narrow about,
  rather than deleted or left standing. The three values are re-derived.
- `marketplace-preview-namespace-3546.test.tsx` carried the larger pin: all ten
  packs, plus the premise that each unit was reused from `common.itemCount`. Its
  whole count-plus-unit-adjacency premise is re-derived around the property the
  old shape could not have. It keeps the Unicode marker census verbatim, keeps
  the `common.itemCount` vocabulary link (case-folded, because five packs now
  open with that noun), and **gains** a pin that fails if someone reintroduces
  the plural family. Its interpolation census moves from three interpolated keys
  to four — that one line is this repair seen from the placeholder side.

Neither pin was deleted and neither was copied forward. A pin grown around a
defect blocks every attempt to repair it and looks exactly like a healthy pin,
because it is green.

## Ablation

Both legs mutate on disk, prove the mutation landed by grep count in both
directions, and restore with `git checkout HEAD --`, proven by an empty
`git diff HEAD`. No build step is involved: vitest aliases `@object-ui/i18n` to
`packages/i18n/src`, so the suites read source, not `dist`.

- **Revert the call site only** (packs kept): **24 assertions red**, all of them
  in the new render suite — ten packs at one item, ten at three, and the four
  unchanged-pack controls. The two i18n pin files stay **green**, which is the
  shape that matters: the pins alone could never have caught this defect, because
  every old pack value was a perfectly good word on its own.
- **Revert one pack (`ru`) only**: **5 red across all three files** — `ru` at one
  item and at three in the render suite, the interpolation-hole census, the
  re-derived marketplace pin and the re-derived residue pin. That is what shows
  the re-derived pins are live rather than vacuous.

## Verification

Run from the repository root, which is the form this repo's own instructions
hold equal to CI.

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| `vitest run packages/i18n/ packages/app-shell/` | 778 files, 8116 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `type-check` (both packages, incl. `tsconfig.test.json`) | Done, Done |
| `lint` (both packages) | 0 errors (33 + 3026 pre-existing warnings) |
| `check:i18n-keys` | exit 0 — interpolation parity over 2736 call sites |
| `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 — 1 en value changed, 9 packs followed |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | exit 0 (report-only); this key is not listed |
| `check:eager-locale-catalogues` | see the report on the card |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — 0 citations added |
| `check-changeset-presence` | exit 0 — 13 source files, 1 changeset |
| `check:test-path-roots`, the three `vi-mock` gates, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
